oracle_provenance.method: constant-current discharge with a lumped thermal model, peak cell-averaged temperature rise read off the reproduced trace
oracle_provenance.pass_tol_basis: flat 5% of the reference value. The band was written to catch a wrong configuration rather than to grade numerical precision, and on this track a wrong configuration lands ~68% away. #468 measured that the claim did not hold here: with the particle mesh left unstated, PyBaMM's default r_n = r_p = 20 lands +10.47% and the band was separating two resolutions rather than two configurations. Ruled on #488 (2026-08-11, option A): the requirement is stated in instruction.md -- 'Resolve the discretisation well enough that the reported number is grid-converged', the sentence 25 sibling contracts already carry -- and no band, gt_value or tolerance moved.
oracle_provenance.gross_error_tol_basis: 20% of the reference value; diagnostic only, not part of the score
oracle_provenance.ocv_max_deviation_basis: 1.4x the reference run's own worst departure from the evaluator's open-circuit-voltage curve, plus 50 mV
oracle_provenance.gt_type_note: Parameter-set-specific solver reference, not a measurement on a physical cell: the task asks for what this parameterisation predicts.

max_temperature_rise_K.description: Peak cell-averaged temperature rise of the ORegan2022 cell over a constant-current discharge at 0.91C from a full charge, stopped when the terminal voltage first reaches 2.5 V, with the cell free to heat up.
